node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polynomial terms
node.description: Identify polynomial terms, variables, coefficients and constants.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Degree of polynomial
node.description: Identify the degree of a polynomial from the highest exponent of its variable terms.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Add and subtract polynomials
node.description: Add and subtract polynomials by combining like terms.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multiply monomial and polynomial
node.description: Multiply a polynomial by a monomial using distribution and index reasoning.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multiply binomials
node.description: Expand products of two binomials using distribution or area models.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Special products
node.description: Recognise and expand special products such as perfect squares and difference of squares.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Common factor polynomials
node.description: Factor polynomial expressions by identifying common numerical and variable factors.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor by grouping
node.description: Factor polynomial expressions by grouping terms with shared factors.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Quadratic standard form
node.description: Recognise and interpret quadratic expressions in standard form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expand binomial products to quadratics
node.description: Expand binomial products to produce equivalent quadratic expressions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor monic quadratics
node.description: Factor monic quadratic expressions by finding numbers with a given sum and product.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor nonmonic quadratics
node.description: Factor quadratic expressions with leading coefficient not equal to one.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Difference of squares
node.description: Recognise and factor quadratic expressions that are differences of two squares.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Completing square form
node.description: Rewrite quadratic expressions in completed-square form to reveal vertex structure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Solve quadratics by factorisation
node.description: Solve quadratic equations by factorising and using the zero-product property.

node.subject: Mathematics

node.description: Solve quadratic equations that can be isolated as a square equal to a number.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Solve quadratics by completing square
node.description: Solve quadratic equations by rewriting them in completed-square form.

node.label: Quadratic formula
node.description: Use the quadratic formula to solve quadratic equations and interpret roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Discriminant
node.description: Use the discriminant to determine the number and type of real roots of a quadratic equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parabola features
node.description: Identify vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts and direction of opening in quadratic graphs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertex form transformations
node.description: Use vertex form to describe translations, stretches, reflections and the vertex of a quadratic function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polynomial like terms have same powers
node.description: Like polynomial terms have the same variable part and same exponents.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Degree is highest exponent
node.description: The degree of a single-variable polynomial is the highest exponent with a nonzero coefficient.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distribution multiplies all terms
node.description: When multiplying a polynomial by a factor, the factor multiplies every term in the polynomial.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard form coefficients define quadratic
node.description: The coefficients in standard form determine the shape, direction and position of a quadratic graph.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factors give roots by zero product
node.description: If a product is zero, at least one factor is zero, which connects factorisation to quadratic roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Completing square reveals vertex
node.description: Completed-square form reveals the vertex and symmetry of a quadratic function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Discriminant classifies roots
node.description: The discriminant indicates whether a quadratic equation has two, one or no real roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertex lies on axis of symmetry
node.description: The vertex of a parabola lies on its axis of symmetry.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Roots are x intercepts
node.description: Real roots of a quadratic equation correspond to x-intercepts of the related quadratic graph.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertex form shows transformations
node.description: Vertex form shows how a basic parabola has been shifted, reflected or stretched.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Add exponents when adding terms
node.description: Learner incorrectly adds exponents when adding like terms instead of adding coefficients.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distribute to first polynomial term only
node.description: Learner multiplies only the first term of a polynomial when expanding a product.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor sum and product reversed
node.description: Learner chooses factor-pair numbers without matching the required sum and product conditions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Quadratic formula sign error
node.description: Learner loses the negative sign or plus-minus structure when using the quadratic formula.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertex is always origin
node.description: Learner assumes every parabola has its vertex at the origin or on the y-axis.

edge.rationale: Polynomial operations require identifying polynomial terms and coefficients.
Degree is an important structural feature of polynomial expressions.
Adding and subtracting polynomials directly practises polynomial operations.
Multiplying a monomial and polynomial is a central polynomial operation.
Binomial multiplication develops polynomial expansion skills.
Special products are common polynomial expansion patterns.
Factoring common factors is a foundational polynomial factorisation strategy.
Grouping is an extension strategy for factorising polynomial expressions.
Standard form is a core representation of quadratic expressions.
Expanding binomial products commonly produces quadratic expressions.
Factoring monic quadratics is a core quadratic-expression skill.
Factoring nonmonic quadratics extends quadratic factorisation.
Difference of squares is a key quadratic factorisation form.
Completed-square form transforms quadratic expressions to reveal structure.
Solving by factorisation is a core quadratic-equation method.
Square-root solving applies to quadratics in squared form.
Completing the square is a major method for solving quadratics.
The quadratic formula is a general method for solving quadratic equations.
The discriminant classifies roots of quadratic equations.
Parabola features are central to analysing quadratic functions.
Vertex-form transformations analyse families of quadratic functions.
Polynomial terms extend algebraic term, coefficient and constant structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify coefficients, constants or variable parts.

edge.rationale: Degree requires recognising variable powers within polynomial terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses the largest coefficient rather than highest exponent.

edge.rationale: Polynomial addition and subtraction require collecting like terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner combines unlike terms or changes exponents while adding.

edge.rationale: Multiplying a monomial and polynomial directly applies distribution.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies only one term inside the polynomial.

edge.rationale: Binomial multiplication extends distribution across multiple terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner omits middle terms or fails to distribute each term.

edge.rationale: Special products are structured cases of binomial multiplication.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a squared binomial as the sum of squared terms only.

edge.rationale: Common-factor polynomial factorisation extends factoring out common factors in expressions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds a numeric common factor but misses variable factors.

edge.rationale: Grouping requires identifying common factors in grouped terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner groups terms without producing a common binomial factor.

edge.rationale: Recognising standard-form quadratics requires identifying degree two polynomial structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot distinguish linear, quadratic and higher-degree expressions.

edge.rationale: Quadratic expansion commonly comes from multiplying binomials.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expands products without generating the middle term.

edge.rationale: Factoring monic quadratics reverses binomial expansion structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds factors with the product but not the required sum.

edge.rationale: Nonmonic quadratic factorisation extends monic factorisation with a leading coefficient.
edge.failure_signal: Learner ignores the leading coefficient when choosing binomial factors.

edge.rationale: Difference of squares is a special product and factorisation pattern.
edge.failure_signal: Learner fails to recognise two square terms separated by subtraction.

edge.rationale: Completing the square transforms a standard-form quadratic into vertex-revealing form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the coefficient structure needed for a square binomial.

edge.rationale: Solving by factorisation requires rewriting the quadratic as a product of factors.
edge.failure_signal: Learner factorises but does not set each factor to zero.

edge.rationale: Solving quadratics by square roots requires square-root and surd reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives only the positive square root or mishandles irrational roots.

edge.rationale: Solving by completing the square requires rewriting in completed-square form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner completes the square but cannot solve the resulting square equation.

edge.rationale: The quadratic formula can be derived from completing the square, though it may be taught procedurally after other methods.
edge.failure_signal: Learner substitutes coefficients without understanding the formula structure.

edge.rationale: The discriminant is the expression under the square root in the quadratic formula.
edge.failure_signal: Learner computes the discriminant but cannot interpret the number of real roots.

edge.rationale: Parabola-feature analysis builds on recognising the quadratic graph shape.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies a parabola but cannot locate vertex, intercepts or symmetry.

edge.rationale: Vertex-form transformations require interpreting vertex and shape features of parabolas.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes an equation but cannot predict graph movement.
